notes.title: Haggar

notes.body:
Kohl’s Strategy: Dockers vs. Haggar Positioning

Key Retailer Question

Why should Kohl’s buy Dockers in addition to Haggar?

  • Need clear differentiation between brands
  • Avoid overlap, especially in “Stretch / Sport / Performance” space
  • Define unique role for Dockers within Kohl’s assortment
Brand Positioning

Haggar (Current State)

  • Moving to $38 price point
  • Primary focus: Haggar Sport / performance-driven product
  • Established in:
    • Stretch
    • Comfort
    • Ease of wear
  • Feels more active / functional

Dockers (Opportunity)

Core Direction:

  • Anchor in Dress Casual
  • Expand Dockers GO, but clearly differentiated
  • Lean into classic styling vs. modern/performance aesthetic

Key Positioning:

  • More refined casual
  • Less “sport,” more everyday polished
Product Strategy

Dockers Focus Areas

  • Technology integration (but elevated)
    • PU
    • Stretch
    • Ratchet systems
  • Must feel intentional and disguised, not overtly technical

Styling Direction

  • More classic than modern
  • Avoid overly sleek / futuristic cues
  • Introduce:
    • Harness styling (casual)
    • Elevated trims and finishes

Belt Innovation

  • Move into:
    • Ratchet
    • Stretch braid w/ backer
    • Track lock systems (important for Kohl’s)
Design Challenge

How do we design Dockers in track lock without feeling too modern?

Guidelines:

  • Softer silhouettes
  • Traditional buckle-inspired hardware
  • Subtle tech integration (hidden functionality)
  • Materials that read:
    • Matte
    • Brushed
    • Heritage-inspired
Dockers GO vs. Haggar Sport

Challenge

  • Avoid direct overlap between:
    • Dockers GO
    • Haggar Sport

Proposed Approach

  • Haggar Sport

    • Primary performance / stretch story
    • More active positioning

  • Dockers GO

    • Still comfort-driven, but:
      • Cleaner
      • More lifestyle-oriented
      • Less “athletic” feeling
Hardware & Design Direction
  • Develop new hardware language
    • Must feel:
      • Dress casual
      • Elevated
  • Avoid:
    • High-shine modern metals
    • Overly technical visual cues
  • Focus on:
    • Brushed finishes
    • Classic buckle cues integrated into ratchet systems
Retail Strategy Insight
  • Kohl’s = strong track lock opportunity
  • Must present Dockers as:
    • A trade-up alternative
    • Not a duplication of Haggar
Next Steps
  • Align internally with:
    • Mark
    • Jenny Dunne
    • Askey R

Working Session Goals

  • Define:
    • Dockers product architecture
    • Clear separation vs. Haggar
    • Hardware direction
    • Track lock design language

notes.title: QUESTIONS

notes.body:
The "Women’s" Growth Engine

The most striking metric in the data is the disparity in growth between divisions. While the men's segment is stable at 8%, women’s is surging at 20%.

The Point: As we move toward Fall '27, there is a clear mandate to lean into the women's category to capture this momentum. We should be looking at how "Amaze" and "ROC" logic can be applied to further capture this demographic.

Transitioning to "Urban Relevance"

There is a strategic pivot toward making the brand "cooler" in urban centers and for urban retailers (like DSG and Scheels).

The Point: The design language is shifting from purely rugged/outdoor to "Elevated Utility" and "Technically Fashionable." This means performance features need to be discreet—think "hidden tech" rather than "overt tech." The goal is to make the product credible on the trail but stylish enough for the city.

Performance Powerhouses: ROC & Amaze

The growth numbers for the ROC (+106%) and Amaze (+208%) collections are massive.

The Point: These aren't just successful products; they are the new blueprints. The fact that the ROC pant is moving at a higher price point ($90) without being on sale shows that consumers are willing to pay for quality and fit (specifically the "Rockband Waistband"). We should double down on these "Fabric Platforms" rather than one-off styles.

The Year-Round PHG Shift

2027 marks the first year that PHG (Hunting) will be a year-round offering.

The Point: This is a significant operational and merchandising change. We need to focus on "Washed Down Camo" and "Saddle Point 2.0" to ensure the transition from a seasonal niche to a year-round lifestyle category is seamless, particularly in the farm and fleet channels like Tractor Supply.

The "October 15" North Star

Looking at the calendar, the timeline is tight.

The Point: We have a hard deadline for COPA Approval by October 15, 2026. This is the critical gatekeeper for the Sales Meetings in late October. To stay on track, the internal "First Adopt" needs to be
notes.title: KEY MEETING TAKEAWAYS

notes.body:
Columbia Sportswear: Strategy, Design & Performance Notes

Core Brand Identity

  • Defining Principle: Performance Obsessed.

  • Pro Line: Titanium (The premier/pro-level offering).

Apparel Design & Macro Trends

  • Wilderness Wellness: Focus on health and the outdoors.

  • Play Everyday: Versatility for daily activity.

  • Technically Fashionable: Merging high-performance specs with aesthetic appeal.

4 Key Design Trends:

  1. Elevated Utility: Adaptive, functional, and discreet performance features.

  2. Ease State: Performance-to-lifestyle transition; relaxed bottoms continue to trend.

  3. Sets: From ski-wear to sweats, coordinated sets remain a major statement.

  4. Return to Color: Focused on "Nostalgic Joy" and "Nature As" palettes.

Fabric Platforms

  • Primary Goal: Warm, Dry, Protected.

  • Soft Touch: Sensorial, soft, and comforting textures.

  • Amaze Puff: Fabric availability for Men’s and Boys'.

  • Hard Work: Protective, functional, and durable materials.

  • ROC (Rigged Outdoor Collection): Exploring belts working directly with this collection; bridges the gap between outdoor performance and rugged workwear.

Seasonal Color & Palettes

  • Q3 (Autumn Trails): Early Fall.

  • Q4 (Winter Dreams): Peak Winter.

  • Volume Drivers: Pond, Mystery, and Nocturnal Red represent the "Dollar" colors.

  • Core Base: Black accounts for 70% of the assortment.

Sub-Brand Focus:

  • PFG (Performance Fishing Gear): Assortment shrinks in Fall. Palette is "Fair Winds"—dusty tones, though brights remain essential. Key colors: Siberia, Bold Orange, Dockside Blue.

  • PHG (Performance Hunting Gear): Additional deck updates pending.

Patterns & Consumer Macro Trends

  • Countryside Craft: Handcrafted, rustic aesthetics.

  • Camo Mash: Mixing and layering different camouflage patterns.

  • Plaid Mania: Heavy trend focus on checks.

  • Ornamental Nature: Decorative animal and nature-inspired prints.

  • Hierarchy: Clear "Good/Better/Best" distinctions across the range.

Business Strategy & Pillars

Strategic Pillars:

  • Own the Trail

  • Dominate Warm

  • Power PFG

  • Fuel Outdoor Lifestyle

  • Accelerate Footwear

Growth Strategy ("Next Level"):

  • Core Strength: Focus on the "Everyday Enthusiast" and "Sensitive Style."

  • Key Market: China (Current leader in the active/outdoor space).

  • 3 Drivers: Credibility, Relevance, Style.

  • Urban Reach: Must increase brand "cool factor" and relevance in urban retail centers.

Performance Results & Metrics

  • ROC Collection: +106% growth ($90 price point, high retention, "Rockband Waistband").

  • Amaze Collection: +208% growth.

  • Product Categories: Dry (+10%), Cool (+37%), Omni-Max Footwear (+55%), Sun Protection (+10%).

  • Demographics: Women’s growth (20%) significantly outpacing Men’s (8%).

    • Market Share: Men’s 48%, Women’s 40%, Youth 8%.

Fall 2027 Planning

  • Fuel Outdoor Lifestyle: Amaze Men’s launching; addition of Amaze Sweats, Youth, and Accessories (Faux Fur Bomber).

  • Timberline Tough: Expansion of rugged jackets and parkas.

  • Fishing/Hunting:

    • PFG: Rolling out "Second Layer & Terminal Tech" through F27.

    • PHG: Moving to a year-round model in 2027. Key trend: "Washed Down Camo" (Soft hand knits). Focus on the Farm channel (Tractor Supply) and Spring goods (Academy).

Merchandising & Retail (North America)

  • Wholesale: Focus on DSG (Dick's Sporting Goods) and Scheels for growth.

  • DTC Footprint: 187 total locations (150 Outlets, 25 Branded Stores, 6 Employee Stores, 2 E-comm).

  • E-commerce: Content engagement is up +56% YoY. Strategy focuses on site personalization and high-volume search terms like "Stocking Stuffers."

Fall 2027 Calendar

MilestoneDate RangeLine Plan Review02/01/26 – 02/28/26
COPA Approval 06/15/26 – 10/15/26 (Final Target)
First Adopt (Internal)06/19/26
Assortment Presentations10/15/26 – 12/31/26
IDR / Sales Meeting10/23/26

Context: Alex Ferreira / Hotdog Hans

  • Alex Ferreira: A two-time Olympic medalist and X Games gold medalist in freestyle skiing.

  • Hotdog Hans: Ferreira’s viral alter ego—a "crusty old man" character who pranks younger skiers by performing professional-level tricks while dressed in vintage gear and denim. Columbia sponsors the content series, leaning into the "relevance" and "style" pillars mentioned in your notes.

notes.body:
Unifi / Repreve – Key Notes & Opportunities

Account Overview

  • Melissa manages:
    • Nike (largest account)
    • Haggar
  • Key regions for sourcing & production:
    • China
    • Vietnam
    • Turkey
    • India
    • North America

Materials & Capabilities

Non-Wovens

  • Sources:
    • Recycled textile waste
    • Recycled plastic bottles (PET)
    • Recycled yarn waste
  • Applications:
    • Wallet interfacing
    • “Chip” is purchased at the non-woven stage
  • Opportunity:
    • Identify factories currently using Repreve in non-wovens
    • Potential for visible liner with sublimation print (PET-based)

Linings

  • Wallet linings:
    • Strong opportunity for recycled content
  • Leather goods:
    • Applies to lining fabrics (e.g., Kate Spade)
  • Concept:
    • Visible interior storytelling using recycled materials

Yarn & Fiber Technologies

  • Repreve tracer technology
    • Embedded “DNA” to verify recycled content authenticity
  • Island of the Sea
    • Single filament
    • 100% recycled yarn
  • Recomfort
    • Acrylic replacement yarn (used in items like beanies)
  • Commodity insight:
    • Polyester & nylon are commoditized (not patentable as yarns themselves)

Specialty Innovations

  • Amy Peppermint

    • Natural deodorizer
    • Extruded directly into fiber (commonly footwear)
    • Permanent (does not wash out)

  • Thermoloop Insulation

    • Only finished product sold by Unifi
    • Made from textile-to-textile (T2T) waste (not post-consumer)
    • Best use:
      • Quilted products (e.g., bags, outerwear)
    • Note:
      • Black is most cost-efficient color for recycling textile waste

Sustainability & Market Position

  • Repreve advantages

    • Credible, recognized supplier for sustainability claims
    • Important when communicating sustainability publicly

  • Retail considerations

    • Costco:
      • May require all materials to be Repreve (especially private label)
      • Canada market is ahead in sustainability requirements

Pricing & Supply Insights

  • Commodity fluctuations:
    • Recycled textile (T2T) = more stable pricing
    • Bottle-based recycling = minimal change
  • Pricing cadence:
    • Updated once per year
  • Note:
    • T2T starts at a higher base cost

Development Process

  • Typical workflow:
    • Brand nominates mill
    • Unifi collaborates directly with mill to develop materials
  • Support:
    • Unifi can provide mill contacts
  • Execution:
    • Design team works with:
      • Mill or
      • Factory
    • Example:
      • Request Repreve for webbing (e.g., for belts)

Key Brand / Market Examples

  • Arcade Belts
    • Uses 100% Repreve
  • Potential applications:
    • Wallets
    • Belts
    • Bag linings
    • Quilted product categories

Events & Industry Touchpoints

  • Intertextile Shanghai
    • Aug 25–27
    • Melissa will be attending

Key Open Questions / Opportunities

  • Is there an existing list of:
    • Factories using Repreve non-wovens?
  • How can we:
    • Integrate visible recycled features (liners, prints)?
    • Expand use in wallet linings + belt components?
  • Where can Thermoloop insulation fit into accessories (beyond apparel)?
